intro: In this week's intelligence digest, we explore the evolving landscape of retail and technology, highlighting significant trends such as the anticipated growth of e-commerce driven by AI innovations and the strategic financial maneuvers of major players like Oracle and Amazon. As retailers navigate challenges, including Swatch's sales decline and the closure of Amazon Go, insights into AI applications in logistics and customer engagement reveal a transformative shift in the industry. Additionally, we examine the positive outlook for jewelers and the implications of emerging AI tools for business efficiency.

readOneThing.title: UK retailers forecast ecommerce growth as AI reshapes shopping and delivery

items.title: UK retailers forecast ecommerce growth as AI reshapes shopping and delivery
bullets: UK retailers anticipate significant ecommerce sales growth driven by AI advancements by 2026.
AI innovations are transforming shopping and delivery experiences for consumers and businesses alike.
Retailers must adapt strategies to leverage AI for enhanced customer engagement and operational efficiency.

items.title: Optimistic outlook for Swatch despite sales slide
bullets: Swatch Group faces declining sales due to reduced demand in Asian markets.
Despite challenges, the company maintains a positive outlook for future growth in jewellery.
Retailers should consider strategies to adapt to shifting consumer preferences in Asia.

items.title: Oracle Is Selling $25 Billion of High-Grade Bonds for AI Funding
bullets: Oracle is raising $25 billion through high-grade bonds to enhance AI infrastructure.
This funding strategy follows Meta's $30 billion bond issuance for similar AI initiatives.
Retail and AI strategists should consider the competitive landscape as tech giants invest heavily in AI capabilities.

items.title: Amazon’s $200 Billion Spending Plan Raises Stakes in A.I. Race
bullets: Amazon plans to invest $200 billion in artificial intelligence initiatives, signaling a major industry shift.
Investor concerns arise as Amazon accelerates its AI spending despite a strong holiday performance.
Retail and AI strategists must adapt to heightened competition and innovation driven by Amazon's investments.

items.title: FedEx launches AI-powered tracking and returns tools
bullets: FedEx launched AI-driven tools to enhance tracking and returns for ecommerce retailers.
The new services aim to improve customer communication on websites and apps.
Retailers can leverage these tools to streamline operations and boost customer satisfaction.

items.title: Anthropic’s breakout moment: how Claude cracked AI for business
bullets: Anthropic's AI coding tools are driving significant revenue growth for the company.
Investor interest in Anthropic is increasing due to its successful business applications of AI.
Retail and AI strategists should consider integrating advanced AI tools to enhance operational efficiency.

items.title: 58 Percent of Surveyed Jewelers Report Growth in December
bullets: 58% of jewelers reported sales growth in December, indicating a positive trend in the jewelry market.
Only 18% of jewelers faced losses, suggesting resilience amidst economic challenges.
Retailers should leverage this growth to enhance inventory strategies and customer engagement.

items.title: Amazon Go? It’s gone. And this is why it went.
bullets: Amazon Go stores closed due to unprofitability despite their cutting-edge technology and convenience.
High-resolution cameras tracked customers and products, showcasing Amazon's retail innovation.
Retailers must reassess technology investments to ensure profitability alongside innovation.
